title: Deviation investigation SOP compliance review packet
description: Compare synthetic deviation-investigation exports with an invented versioned SOP checklist and prepare an administrative gap register and draft review queue.

sample_policy.description: The checklist, due dates, priorities, evidence types, and decision precedence are invented sample policy. Administrative completeness is not investigation approval, deviation closure, product disposition, or a regulatory conclusion.

golden_provenance.author: Health and life sciences scenario owner
golden_provenance.description: All five expected results and case derivations were authored from HOW_TO.md before baseline execution. Dates, applicable SOP versions, required evidence, reason codes, queue order, and totals were calculated manually; no baseline output supplied expected values.

cases.derivation: SOP version 1 applies to all three deviations. SYN-DEV-001 is minor, age 20, on track, and has all three applicable evidence types. SYN-DEV-002 is major, age 41, overdue, and lacks approval and impact assessment; its existing impact task suppresses only that draft reason. SYN-DEV-003 is critical, age 29, due soon, has no investigation, and lacks all five applicable requirements. High-priority queue order is deviation ID. Counts and all nested evidence references were written manually.

A deviation opened exactly on 2026-07-01 selects SOP version 2, not version 1. At as_of 2026-07-09 its 2026-07-11 due date is due soon. Identical root-cause evidence rows collapse. Approval evidence recorded on 2026-07-10 is future evidence, so approval remains missing and the deviation requires review.

The closed minor deviation has both version-1 requirements and is administratively complete. It opened 2026-02-01, was due 2026-02-11 under the ten-day sample policy, and completed 2026-02-15, so late completion remains a review reason without changing the completeness classification or approving the investigation.
The as_of_date 2026-02-30 is not a real Gregorian date. The packet is rejected before joins with one invalid-field exception and empty outputs.

Two evidence rows share SYN-E-CONFLICT but assert different evidence types. A primary identifier cannot represent both facts, so the complete packet is rejected rather than selecting the first or last row.
